what_changed: ⭐ PUB-ASO REACHES 7/7 ON publish_bar AT PIN 3d5c709b69bc. Clause 2 closed on a PREFLIGHT_FULL=1 run that came back EXIT=0 with PINNED_SHA=3d5c709b6 and no +dirty suffix; clauses 1 and 6 closed on round 34. The non-zero exit code is the AUTHORITY line, which correctly refuses to auto-ship a paper trimcrae excluded from the aiXiv grant by name — that is the bar working, not a failure.

ROUND 34: six blind seats — arithmetic, statistics, citations-and-archive, scope-and-language, hostile-referee, regression — on one pinned commit. ZERO BLOCKERS across all six. Seven P1s, every one a coverage gap rather than a wrong sentence, and thirty P2s. Records filed at research/autonomy/review-seats/PUB-ASO-3d5c709b69bc…{-seat-<lens>.json ×6, and the roll-up}, hardening state generated by record_bar_evidence.

research/autonomy/publish_bar.py — CLAUSES 1 AND 6 NOW IDENTIFY A REVIEW BY WHAT IT READ RATHER THAN BY WHEN IT HAPPENED. `record['reviewed_commit'] == sha` becomes `_covers()`: exact sha match short-circuits, otherwise the DELIVERABLE DIGESTS at the two commits are compared. Clause 6 additionally searches for a roll-up filed at another commit that covers this one, and refuses when two do. Declared in amendments.jsonl with the self_serving_check answered at length. This is AUT-PD-205-d7df5340, filed by the previous cycle and deliberately not landed by it.

research/autonomy/autonomy-state.json — the subagent width cap lifted on trimcrae's instruction ('There shouldn't be a limit on parallel subagents'), live dial and declared posture raised together so the governor cannot read the change as the loop loosening its own hold. The rest of budget_hold is untouched: active stays true, floor_backoff_level stays 2, and the interval, items-per-cycle and cycles-per-session ceilings keep their pre-sprint values.

research/autonomy/round34-prepin-seat/ — the seat that reviewed the right bytes at the wrong commit, preserved outside the directory the bar globs, with a README recording the ordering rule that would have avoided it.

research/autonomy/research-ledger.json — AUT-PROP-057 and AUT-PD-205 closed; AUT-PD-206-91c8e949-60cbbacf files round 34's seven P1s, the P2s that are real defects, and one defect in the loop itself; AUT-PROP-055 and AUT-PROP-056 declared requires_trimcrae:false; a dead seat's lease released with the evidence for the release.
_the_process_finding_this_cycle_was_actu: ⛔⛔ trimcrae, 2026-09-02, after watching 41 minutes go into closing a handful of blockers: 'None of that makes any sense to me. This is getting way too complex. This is not a good process. Be smart and fix it.' ★ THE MEASUREMENT THAT ANSWERED HIM: across the 104 commits between round 32's pin and this cycle, PUB-ASO's deliverable digest held ONE value. There were no blockers and had been none for 104 commits; the time was going into manufacturing fresh commit shas, because clauses 1 and 6 compared shas and any commit anywhere — a ledger header, a test-selector hash — discarded a clean six-seat round. Two of this cycle's own 41 minutes are the proof: PREFLIGHT_FULL went red on a STALE SELECTOR RECORD, a file with nothing to do with the paper, and fixing it moved the pin and voided a 25-minute seat. ⚠ AND THE THIRD CAUSE WAS MINE: I pinned before proving the gate green on that tree. The order is green the gate, THEN pin, THEN seat it, and it is now written into research/autonomy/round34-prepin-seat/README.md where the next session will hit it.
_blocked_by_empty_means: Nothing refused this cycle. The one thing that could have — amendment_guard on publish_bar.py, since clause 1 was blocking this very session — was answered rather than routed around: the authority for the change is trimcrae's explicit instruction, it is a re-anchoring rather than a relaxation (all 35 existing bar guards pass unchanged, an exact sha match still short-circuits, an unbuildable digest fails closed), and it did not unblock the cycle that made it — PUB-ASO still read 5/7 immediately afterwards, with clause 1 still failing on the width ratchet, which round 34 then cleared by looking.
queued_next: AUT-PD-206-91c8e949-60cbbacf — round 34's open findings. The two that several blind seats reached independently are the abstract's unguarded scope sentence and the Supplementary Information addressing the extended report rather than the journal article. ⛔ Every paper edit moves the deliverable digest and costs a fresh six-seat round, so batch them into one edit pass, one regeneration and one round.

subagents.why: Seven blind seats launched over the cycle. The first ran alone at the then-governed width of 1 and reviewed a pin this round later abandoned (record preserved in round34-prepin-seat/). A second ran alone at the real pin. The remaining FIVE were launched CONCURRENTLY in one message after trimcrae lifted the width dial in session — 'There shouldn't be a limit on parallel subagents' — recorded in autonomy-state.json under `_subagent_width_LIFTED_BY_TRIMCRAE_2026_09_02`, live dial and declared posture raised together. So the widest concurrent moment was 5. All seven were read-only in the repository, each with its own seat-prefixed scratch directory, and each was told that blindness is a property of its commands rather than its intentions and that a leak must be DISCLOSED rather than discarded. Three disclosed one.

notes:
1 ⛔ THE HARNESS REPORTED A RED GATE AS EXIT 0. The first PREFLIGHT_FULL run's task notification said 'completed (exit code 0)'; the log's own marker said EXIT=1. Reading the marker rather than the reported code is the only reason the failure was caught, and it is the third instrument in this repository whose reported value and real value have diverged.
2 ⚠ A CONCURRENT SESSION HELD THE TRUNK THROUGHOUT. origin/main moved under this cycle repeatedly; one merge conflicted on the ledger and on autonomy-state.json and was resolved by taking the trunk's copy of both files whole and re-applying this cycle's two edits by hand, rather than by hand-merging JSON — the duplicate-id risk from a hand merge is worse than the cost of redoing the edits. That session also allocated the ordinal CYC-0091 with its own discriminator; both receipts are genuinely the Nth cycle and the discriminator is what keeps them from colliding.
3 ⛔ THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION OF THE DIGEST FIX WAS WRONG IN THE PERMISSIVE DIRECTION AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REVERTED. Pooling every seat that ever read the same bytes into one round made clause 1 pass sooner. It merges rounds 31 and 32 — the digest a6f7158552096aea covers both, ten seats — and it makes the clause unsatisfiable, because a superseded round's blocker could then be cleared only by changing the paper even where the defect it names is in a file the paper does not ship. Caught by running the bar and reading the refusal, then pinned by a test that a mutation showed was too weak to see it.
4 ⚠ THE PERMISSION CLASSIFIER REFUSED ROUGHLY A DOZEN CALLS INTERMITTENTLY — heredocs, `sed -i`, `python3 -c` with a write, and twice a plain command it had already allowed. The repository's own tooling ran; work continued through the Edit and Write tools. Recorded because a future session hitting it should not read it as a repository fault. The previous cycle recorded the same thing.
5 ⚠ ONE SEAT'S 25 MINUTES WERE SPENT ON A PIN THIS ROUND ABANDONED, AND THAT IS MY ERROR, NOT THE GATE'S. Its record is preserved and its verdict of no blockers on byte-identical text is why the pin was allowed to stand instead of the paper being edited first.
6 ⛔ `ready_to_post --new` PRINTS 'nothing new' WHILE THE BAR READS 7/7, and the reason is structural rather than a bug in this cycle: it evaluates at HEAD, clause 2 binds a receipt to a sha, and a round's evidence lands after the commit that run gated. Filed in AUT-PD-206 and deliberately NOT fixed here, because this cycle is the one whose paper would be announced. trimcrae was told directly in session instead, which research-loop §5 says is the deliverable the queue file only exists to make checkable.
